newsitem.title: UK: Russian loans higher on London Club news.
newsitem.headline: Russian loans higher on London Club news.

text.p: Russian Vnesheconombank loans were sharply higher on Wednesday on news Russia had made significant progress in reconciling its debt owed to commercial bank creditors, emerging market debt sources said.

"The Russian market has been strong on the back of the news coming out of the discussions in Frankfurt. I think it is generally seen as positive," said Philip Poole, director of research for Eastern Europe at ING Barings in London.
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were one percentage point higher at 88-1/4 bid and its mark loans RUVNDMLNS were one percentage point firmer at 93-3/8 bid.

Deutsche Bank AG said earlier in Frankfurt that Vnesheconombank had reported it acknowledged about 80 percent of the bank's claims and that creditors signed reconciliation statements of just under 20 percent of the eligible debt.

"The 80 percent is higher than I would have thought but the 20 percent is a bit lower than I would have expected," said Poole. But he added, "On balance, I think it is positive. It does show things are moving ahead." "I believe the deal will happen and I believe the deal will close towards the end of September," he said.
In addition, Deutsche said documentation of the Vnesheconombank rescheduling had been finalized and it will now be sent to the Russian government for its formal approval.
In the Latin Brady market, Brazilian debt prices were higher following news Brazil priced $3.0 billion of 30-year bonds at 395 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Brazil also announced it had exchanged $1.622 billion in principal amount for discount bonds, $542 million for pars and $86 million for C bonds.
Brazilian Discount bonds BRFLTD24=RR were 3/8 higher at
83-1/4 bid and its "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/8 firmer at 79-1/2 bid.
